EVALUATE BEFORE YOU RELY

Has your model met the target?

Check accuracy, the strength of the evidence, and consistency across training runs.

How to use this evaluator

Go to the assessment ↓

This page checks predictions from an already-trained binary classifier; it does not train your model. Choose which outcome counts as positive (1)—for example, “machine fails within 24 hours.” The other outcome is negative (0).

  1. Bring the answers and predictions. Import JSON containing the known outcome and your model’s prediction for each unseen example. Use “Download example JSON” below for the format.
  2. Set your requirements. Decide which errors are acceptable before inspecting the final test. Select the model run chosen using validation data.
  3. Read all three results. Classification checks the selected run; stability compares training runs; reproducibility checks whether identical training setups produced matching model artifacts.

What is a seed? A seed is a number used to control training randomness, such as starting weights or the order of examples. Train with seeds 11, 22, and 33 to see whether results stay consistent. Repeat seed 11 with the same setup to check reproducibility. A larger seed is not better, and fixing the seed alone does not guarantee identical training.

What do the acceptance criteria mean?
CriterionMeaning and example
Minimum accuracyCorrect predictions out of all examples. If 90 of 100 predictions are right, accuracy is 90%. A common negative class can make accuracy look high even when every positive is missed.
Minimum precisionCorrect positive predictions out of all positive predictions. If 80 of 100 warnings are justified, precision is 80%. Higher precision means fewer wasted warnings.
Minimum recallDetected positives out of all actual positives. If the model detects 90 of 100 at-risk examples, recall is 90%. Higher recall means fewer missed cases.
Maximum false-positive rateIncorrect positive predictions out of all actual negatives. Ten false warnings among 1,000 healthy examples is a 1% false-positive rate. This is different from the share of warnings that are wrong.
Require the 95% intervalAccount for sampling uncertainty. For a 90% minimum target, a 92% score with an 88–95% interval is insufficient evidence. The lower bound must clear a minimum target; the upper bound must stay below a maximum. With this option off, only the measured score is checked.
Minimum distinct seedsHow many different recorded training seeds must be present. Three runs with seeds 11, 22, and 33 count as three; repeating seed 11 three times counts as one. One trained model can be assessed for performance, but cannot establish training stability.
Maximum accuracy spreadThe highest run accuracy minus the lowest, in percentage points. Accuracies of 91%, 92%, and 94% have a spread of 3 points. Stability also requires every run to meet the minimum point accuracy target.

The 95% Wilson intervals on this page assume independent, representative examples and apply separately to each metric. They are not a 95% probability that an individual prediction is correct. Correlated readings or repeated subjects require a grouped or time-aware evaluation.

How should I read the output?
Pass
The relevant requirements are met for the supplied data. The overall result passes only when classification, stability, and reproducibility all pass.
Fail
A measured score misses its target, training variation exceeds the allowed limit, or comparable model artifacts differ. Any failed area makes the overall result fail.
Insufficient evidence
No check in that area has failed, but the evidence is incomplete—for example, a confidence interval crosses the target, a metric has no denominator, there are too few seeds, or reproducibility metadata is missing. This is not a pass.

The error grid: true positives are correct warnings; false positives are false warnings; false negatives are missed positive cases; true negatives are correctly rejected negative cases. Prediction agreement shows how often different runs give the same answer to the same example; agreement alone does not mean the answer is correct.

Reproducibility needs extra evidence. Supply repeated runs with the same seed and matching fingerprints (SHA-256 hashes) of the data, training recipe, and environment. Their model artifact hashes must match. The page compares submitted hashes; it does not independently rerun or audit the training. Good scores can therefore coexist with “Not established.”

Validation is provisional. Use validation data to select a model and tune settings, then use a separate untouched test set for final acceptance. A pass applies to these data and requirements; it does not guarantee future performance.

What should my input file contain?

Use a JSON object with split set to test or validation, and a runs array. Each run needs a unique id, an integer seed for stability checks, and rows containing sample_id, y_true (known outcome), and y_pred (predicted outcome). Both labels must be numeric 0 or 1. Convert model scores to labels using a decision threshold chosen on validation data.

Every run must use the same sample IDs and known outcomes. Import predictions, not model weights. Files are evaluated in your browser, up to 10 MB and 50 runs. “Export assessment” downloads the metrics, rules, and verdicts; it does not export a trained model.

REPEATED TRAINING

Accuracy by run

Stability requires every run to meet the point accuracy target, enough distinct seeds, and an acceptable score spread.

ERROR PATTERNS

Where predictions go wrong

Positive class = 1. Recall measures detected positives. False-positive rate measures negatives incorrectly flagged.

REPRODUCIBILITY

What counts as reproducibility evidence?

Provide two runs with the same seed, data hash, training recipe hash, and environment hash. Their model artifact hashes must match. All hashes must be SHA-256. This checks submitted evidence; it does not independently execute or audit your training environment.

"metadata": {
  "data_sha256": "64 hex characters",
  "recipe_sha256": "64 hex characters",
  "environment_sha256": "64 hex characters",
  "model_sha256": "64 hex characters"
}
Evidence, not a guarantee. A pass applies to these data and rules. Validation results are provisional. This tool does not certify clinical safety or trading profitability. Method & limitations ↓
